description:
Redwood Inference is running a cross-language SDK parity initiative to make Python, TypeScript, and Go SDK behavior consistent and predictable for production usage—specifically around authentication, retries/backoff, timeouts, and streaming semantics. The immediate goal is to reduce customer friction ("works in TS but not in Python"), lower support volume for intermittent failures (timeouts/429/5xx/stream disconnects), and ensure Redwood’s platform reliability features (rate limiting, Retry-After, request IDs, idempotency guidance) are surfaced uniformly across SDKs.

Goals & deliverables:
- Produce a parity audit matrix covering auth sources/precedence, default timeouts, retryable errors, backoff/jitter, max attempts, and streaming edge cases.
- Define and approve a single standard for: (1) auth resolution order (explicit param vs env vars), (2) error taxonomy and typed errors, (3) retry policy (status codes, network errors, respect Retry-After, exponential backoff with jitter), (4) timeout model (connect/read/overall), and (5) streaming behavior (disconnect handling, partial output, retry guidance, idempotency).
- Implement changes across redwood-sdk-python, redwood-sdk-typescript, and redwood-sdk-go with a shared conformance test suite and fixtures.
- Update docs, quickstarts, and examples to show the same configuration knobs and recommended defaults.
- Add usage analytics/telemetry hooks (where permitted) or at minimum standardized logging fields (request_id, retry_count, timeout_ms, streaming_disconnect_reason) to support debugging and observability.

Scope:
- In scope: API key/Bearer token auth, environment variable naming/precedence, request headers, retry/backoff configuration, timeouts, streaming client behavior, typed errors, documentation and examples, release notes, and migration notes.
- Out of scope: major API surface redesign, new auth mechanisms beyond existing keys/tokens, and deep changes to model semantics. Gateway changes are limited to improving consistency signals (e.g., Retry-After, error codes) rather than new product features.

Stakeholders:
- DRI (DevEx): Monica Patel (Director, SDK Engineering)
- Tech lead: Ibrahim Khan (Staff SWE, SDKs)
- Language owners: Dana Lo (TS), Mateusz Zielinski (Go), Sabrina James (Python/examples)
- Dependencies/partners: Kaitlyn Nguyen + Ethan Park (platform/auth integration), Allison Grant + SRE leadership (retry/timeout standards and observability), Marcus Lin (security review for auth defaults and secret handling), Henry Cho (PM for API ergonomics), Docs team via eng-developer-experience/docs-site

Timeline (targeted over ~8 weeks):
1) Audit & data gathering (Week 1–2): parity matrix, top support issues, reproduce incidents, draft standard.
2) Design & approval (Week 2–3): RFC/ADR(s), security/SRE signoff, migration plan.
3) Implementation (Week 3–6): SDK updates + conformance tests + docs/examples; staged releases.
4) Rollout & validation (Week 6–8): beta channel, monitor error/timeout metrics, finalize migration guide, retro.

Constraints & risk management:
- Minimize breaking changes; where unavoidable, gate behind opt-in flags and ship deprecation warnings.
- Streaming retry is intentionally conservative (avoid duplicate side effects); document best practices with idempotency keys and server request IDs.
- Ensure auth handling does not increase secret exposure (logging redaction, safe error messages).

files.description: Published overview of the parity initiative: goals, non-goals, timeline, owners, and links to audit matrix, ADRs, and tracking tickets.

Parity matrix documenting current vs desired behavior across Python/TS/Go for auth precedence, retries, timeouts, streaming edge cases, and error typing; includes open questions and acceptance criteria.

Company-wide standard for SDK retry/backoff and timeout behavior (retryable status codes, network errors, Retry-After handling, exponential backoff w/ jitter, max attempts, connect/read/overall timeout semantics).
Security-reviewed guidance for SDK authentication: env var names/precedence, header formats, safe error messages, logging redaction requirements, and recommended secret storage practices.
ADR capturing the final decision on retry policy defaults and configurability (including rationale for streaming retry limitations and idempotency guidance).
ADR selecting the timeout model used across SDKs (overall vs granular connect/read), default values, and how they map to underlying HTTP clients per language.
Draft-to-published migration guide for developers upgrading SDK versions, including deprecated options, behavioral changes, and code snippets per language.
Streaming quickstart updated to reflect standardized streaming events, disconnect handling, timeout configuration, and recommended retry patterns.
SRE/observability analysis of how client retries affect platform load (thundering herd risk), recommended defaults, and monitoring dashboards to watch during rollout.
Summary of support drivers attributable to SDK inconsistencies (e.g., 429 handling, timeouts, stream disconnects), with links to Jira tickets and proposed mitigations.
Working doc used by SDK engineers: raw findings from code reading, repro scripts, links to Slack threads, and a running list of mismatches to resolve.
Sheet-style table (represented as text) tracking each behavior row (auth/retry/timeout/streaming) with per-language columns, status, owner, and target release version.
Experiment notes comparing different backoff/jitter settings under simulated 429/5xx conditions; includes graphs described in text and recommended defaults.
Draft dashboard spec (metrics, dimensions, thresholds) to track retries, timeouts, and streaming disconnects during rollout; includes proposed alert tuning.
PM-facing brief: expected customer impact, rollout plan, comms strategy, and success metrics (support ticket reduction, retry rate changes, SDK upgrade adoption).
Plan for a cross-language conformance suite: shared fixtures, golden error shapes, simulated retryable responses, and how tests run in CI for each SDK.
Personal scratchpad enumerating streaming failure modes (half-closed connections, proxy buffering, server FIN mid-chunk) and what behavior the standard should require.
Release checklist for shipping standardized behavior: versioning, changelog entries, migration notes, CI gates, canary users, and validation steps.
Engineering epic tracking the overall initiative; includes milestones, owners per language, and links to sub-issues, ADRs, and rollout checklist.
Ticket to draft the retry/timeout standard, collect SRE + PM + Security feedback, and publish Confluence standards/ADRs.
Align env var names and precedence across SDKs; includes migration approach and tests to prevent regressions.
Python SDK work item implementing standardized retry/backoff, Retry-After parsing, and consistent error typing; links to PR(s).
TypeScript SDK refactor to unify timeouts and retry plumbing; includes review checklist for backwards compatibility.
Go SDK ticket to harden streaming client behavior (timeouts, cancellation, disconnect detection) and document retry guidance.
Define and implement a shared error taxonomy (names, fields like request_id, status_code, retryable flag) across SDKs.
Build conformance fixtures + CI integration so all SDKs must pass the same behavioral tests for retries/timeouts/errors/streaming.
Update docs site and quickstarts to show consistent auth/retry/timeout configuration examples across languages.
Standardize logging/telemetry fields emitted by SDKs (or surfaced via hooks) for retries/timeouts/stream disconnects to improve debugging.
Platform-facing ticket to ensure API gateway emits consistent Retry-After and error codes/fields used by SDKs; coordination with platform team.
PM ticket covering release notes, migration guide requirements, deprecation messaging, and how to announce changes without alarming customers.
Rollout ticket: beta releases, internal dogfooding, monitoring dashboards, and defined rollback triggers.
Create/update support troubleshooting guidance for retries/timeouts/streaming (how to ask for request_id, how to tune timeouts) and link in Confluence support-top-issues.
Retro ticket to capture what worked/failed, follow-ups, and any remaining parity gaps.
PR aligning Python SDK auth resolution (explicit client param vs env vars), updating docsstrings, and adding redaction-safe error messages.
PR implementing retry defaults (429/5xx/network), exponential backoff with jitter, respecting Retry-After, and exposing configuration knobs.
PR adding consistent timeout model to Python SDK and mapping it to the underlying HTTP client; includes migration notes and tests.
PR improving streaming iterator behavior on disconnects (typed exception w/ request_id, partial output semantics) and documenting retry guidance.
PR adding parity conformance test runner + fixtures to Python SDK CI, including simulated 429/Retry-After cases.
PR refactoring TS retry middleware to match the standard error taxonomy (retryable flag, request_id propagation) and align retryable codes.
PR standardizing timeouts in TS SDK, wiring AbortController correctly for streaming vs non-streaming requests, and documenting edge cases.
PR adding Retry-After parsing for both seconds/date formats and adding jittered exponential backoff consistent with other SDKs.
PR clarifying streaming cancellation semantics and ensuring partial output is surfaced consistently; updates examples.
PR aligning TS SDK env vars and precedence with Python/Go, including deprecation warnings for old names.
PR implementing standardized retry policy in Go (retryable errors/codes, backoff/jitter, Retry-After) and exposing options.
PR aligning Go SDK timeouts and ensuring context cancellation consistently aborts HTTP + streaming reads.
PR improving streaming error typing (request_id, status) and documenting safe retry patterns (idempotency considerations).
PR aligning Go auth env vars, header formatting, and ensuring secrets are not logged in debug mode.
PR adding shared conformance harness integration for Go SDK with fixtures for 429/5xx/network failures and streaming interruptions.
PR updating API gateway to consistently emit Retry-After on 429 responses and harmonize error fields consumed by SDKs.
PR ensuring request_id is always present and consistent across streaming and non-streaming error responses (gateway + downstream services).
PR introducing/cleaning up error code enum and documentation so SDKs can reliably classify retryable vs terminal errors.
Docs PR updating retry/timeout pages to show consistent examples for Python/TS/Go and linking to migration notes.
Docs PR updating streaming guide for standardized events, disconnect handling, and recommended timeouts.
Quickstarts PR adding explicit retry/timeout configuration snippets in all language quickstarts with consistent naming.
Examples PR showing safe retry patterns, request_id logging, and streaming cancellation handling.
Observability PR adding dashboard panels/alerts for retry rate, timeout rate, and streaming disconnect reasons during rollout.
PR aligning OpenAI-compat layer error formatting so SDKs see consistent fields/codes regardless of endpoint path.
